summary: IPv6 Path MTU blackhole on site-to-site tunnel causing intermittent gRPC keepalive timeouts and KV cache heartbeats in private deploy
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent gRPC keepalive timeouts from serving nodes in their private deployment. Timeouts primarily impact KV cache heartbeats and short-lived streaming connections, resulting in transient 5xx/connection-reset observed by application.

Impact: Approximately 8% of requests to the customer's serving tier experience ~5-20s stalled tokens or gRPC keepalive timeouts during nightly batch window (higher packet sizes). No model corruption observed, but increased latency and occasional fallback to lower-tier model variants.

Environment: Private deployment (VPC peered to GreenField Health on-prem via site-to-site tunnel). Multi-AZ serving fleet in us-east-1. Customer uses IPv6-only internal addressing on the on-prem side with NAT64 for egress to some external services. Redwood control plane connects over the peered path for artifact fetch and kv heartbeats.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From a serving node in the customer VPC, trigger a large-shard presigned range download or a prompt with long context to force >1200B MTU segments.
2) Observe gRPC keepalive and control-plane heartbeats during sustained transfer (nightly batch).
3) Failures are intermittent — reproduce rate ~1 in 10 under load.

Observed logs/traces:
- serving-node logs: "gRPC: keepalive timeout, closing connection" followed by "kv-cache: heartbeat failed, retrying"
- tcpdump captures show ICMPv6 "Packet too big" messages from an intermediate router but no subsequent PMTU discovery adjustment from the on-prem client stack.
- traceroute6 shows a jump in MTU-limited hop and then subsequent silence on large packets.
- No TLS handshake failures were observed; failures are at gRPC keepalives/stream stalls.

Customer-provided artifacts: attached pcap, traceroute6 output, and sample serving-node logs (uploaded to ticket attachment).
comments: 2026-03-13 09:15 - Customer(ops@greenfield): We're seeing intermittent failures in production during nightly shard fetches. Tokens stall and we see keepalive timeouts. Happening only since last Friday after a router firmware upgrade on the branch site.

2026-03-13 09:42 - Support (Marcus Lee): Thanks for the data — we've triaged and see ICMPv6 'Packet too big' in the pcap. I'm escalating to Network/SRE to verify PMTU behavior across the site-to-site tunnel.

2026-03-13 11:05 - SRE (Priya Nair): Reproduced locally by sending large TCP segments over the tunnel. Observed that intermediate appliance drops fragments for IPv6 and does not forward ICMPv6 PMTU messages to the host. Requesting packet captures from the customer's tunnel egress and the branch router config dump.
2026-03-13 14:20 - Customer(ops@greenfield): Provided router config and tunnel device logs; firmware shows 'frag-offload disabled' option toggled during upgrade.

2026-03-14 08:10 - SRE (Priya Nair): Implemented temporary workaround: forced MSS clamp on the Redwood-serving NAT gateway for this customer route to 1200 bytes to avoid large IPv6 datagrams. Observing immediate reduction in keepalive timeouts in canary nodes. Planning permanent remediation with customer network team.

2026-03-14 12:30 - Engineering (Diego Morales): Reviewed possibility of adding aggressive PMTU probing on our side for IPv6 sessions to detect path MTU changes faster. Raised infra task INT-75921 for a follow-up enhancement.
investigation_notes: Initial inspection focused on TLS/OCSP and presigned artifact downloads; TLS was healthy. Packet captures revealed ICMPv6 'Packet too big' originating from an on-prem transit appliance but on-prem host did not send subsequent smaller packets. Hypothesis: on-prem router's firmware upgrade disabled fragmentation/fragment forwarding or suppressed ICMPv6 PMTU messages toward the client (or rewrote them). Without PMTU feedback, client's IPv6 stack continued to send larger packets leading to silent drops of gRPC keepalive packets during large transfers. Correlation: spikes coincide with nightly large-shard transfers and were reproducible when forcing >1280B payloads over IPv6. Verified that when we clamp MSS to 1200 on egress NAT, failures disappear for canary nodes. Also validated no issues when traffic took IPv4 path (dual-stack fallback). Logged kernel/sysctl state on host — clients didn't respond to PMTU change because ICMPv6 replies were not visible to them. Checked control-plane metrics for KV cache retries and saw spike matching customer reports.
steps_taken: Analyzed customer pcap and traceroute6 outputs
Reached out to customer network team for router config and firmware notes
Reproduced issue in staging by sending large IPv6 payloads over a mirrored tunnel
Applied temporary MSS clamp (1200) on Redwood egress for affected route
Monitored canary nodes for 6 hours — keepalive timeouts dropped from 8%->0.4%
Opened internal follow-up INT-75921 to consider proactive PMTU probing for IPv6 and a runbook update
root_cause: A site-to-site transit appliance/branch router firmware change disabled proper IPv6 PMTU propagation (or dropped ICMPv6 'Packet too big'), causing a path MTU blackhole. Hosts continued sending oversized IPv6 datagrams, resulting in intermittent gRPC keepalive/stall behavior during large transfers.
resolution:
Short-term: temporary MSS clamp to 1200 applied on the Redwood egress NAT for the affected customer route which mitigated the symptom across the fleet. Long-term: customer will coordinate with their network vendor to re-enable ICMPv6 PMTU messages / fix fragmentation behavior. Redwood to add a defensive will-have: optional MSS clamp per-customer-route for private deployments and an IPv6 PMTU probing enhancement (INT-75921). Follow-up actions recorded in the ticket.

Rollout notes: MSS clamp was deployed to the customer's dedicated egress route in two waves (canary then full) during a low-traffic window; no downtime expected. Monitoring dashboards show KPI recovery.

Customer communication: Informed GreenField Health of root cause and remediation steps; awaiting confirmation from their network vendor for permanent fix.
follow_up_tasks: Customer to validate vendor firmware patch and re-enable PMTU/fragmentation behavior
Engineering: implement optional per-route MSS clamp toggle in control plane (INT-75921)
SRE: add IPv6 PMTU detection probe to private-deploy health checks
Docs: update private-deploy runbook for IPv6 PMTU troubleshooting
